hook.line: A marketing expert says you are not allowed to ask her to fix your strategy unless you already do these things.
hook.visual: Motion-blurred frame as she settles close to the phone, then a tight selfie shot; a 3-line white title across the top promises 'these four things' from frame one.

beats.what: Callout line spoken with the four-things title already on screen at the top.
Only early cut: from the close phone framing to a wider seated shot in front of a shelf; this frame holds for most of the video.
Point one, consistency: 'I am your cheerleader, not your babysitter' with open-hand gestures.
Reframe line: consistency that needs motivation is just comfort; personal proof that she stayed consistent in bad times.
Point two, selling every day: listing features like a product manual is describing, not selling.
Point three: marketing that reads like an About page; she names the 'identity' sales-psychology idea.
Point four, urgency: not fake 'only a few spots left', but showing what the audience misses each day.
Cut to the close: asks how many of the four things the viewer already does.

why_it_works: Gatekeeping callout ('you're not allowed to ask me') turns the list into a self-test, so viewers stay to score themselves.
A fixed top title promising four things acts as a progress counter; each 'number two/three' tells the viewer how far they are.
Each point uses a 'you say X, however Y' reversal that names a habit the viewer recognises, which triggers comments.
Ending on 'how many of these do you do?' turns the self-test into a comment prompt.
weaknesses: Three minutes with one framing and only 3 cuts; nothing visual marks the change between points.
Title and handle sit outside the safe area for the whole video (measured outside_safe_share 1.0).
No live captions for 3.48 words/s speech, so muted viewers only get the title.
for_robert: Pin a 'N things' title at the top for the whole reel and let Fred hold up a numbered card (1/4, 2/4...) at each point, giving a long single-shot talk the visual chapter marks this video lacks.
